literal_closed_collar_construction: 19.1 The relative bundle prerequisite is a diagram on an entire CLOSED collar, not merely on its boundary. This is supplied before fitting: extend every already triangulated boundary face by a positive-width radial product collar. For a controller `Y>X`, `pi_X R_Y=pi_X`, so the affine diagram map ignores that collar coordinate. For `Y<X`, `pi_X R_Y=R_Y|X pi_X`, and the fixed target triangulation is extended by the identical `Y` collar operation; the diagram map carries that collar coordinate identically to the base. On multiple-face intersections the radial families commute, giving the same product coordinate maps in either order. Thus `pi_X F=h r` holds throughout the closed collar and `r` is PL after common product subdivision. A smaller collar is protected; the positive-width buffer separates every later fitting support from it. This is the actual collar-neighbourhood hypothesis of the bundle theorem, and not an assertion that its manifold boundary-extension theorem automatically preserves a bundle projection.
